proposals.name: P1: Centered small-step residual symbols (kill mu-law's histogram equalization; mid-gray PNG by construction)
proposals.mechanism: Replace the mu-law-companded full-range symbol map with a linear-in-error quantizer whose OUTPUT is a signed residual symbol centered at the code midpoint: symbol s = clip(round(pct_residual / q_step), -127, 127) stored as uint8 s+128 (or s+32768 for uint16 with 15-bit symbol range). q_step is chosen per-variable from a user error bound (this is exactly SZ3's linear-scale quantization). Values whose |s| exceeds the clip range get an escape code (0 or 255) plus an exact float32 patch stored in a side list in metadata. Crucially this must sit downstream of a good predictor (closed-loop previous-value at minimum), so the symbol distribution is a peaky near-zero-centered Laplacian: the grid becomes a mostly-mid-gray (128) image with texture only where the signal actually changes.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is the single largest information-theoretic lever in the pipeline. Today's mu-law stage is a compander designed for scalar quantization SNR, not for entropy coding: it equalizes the symbol histogram, pushing order-0 entropy to ~7.5-8 bits/symbol, so PNG DEFLATE compresses the 8-bit grid barely below 1 byte/sample (observed lossy ratios 0.05-0.22, barely under lossless Delta+Zstd at 0.12-0.24 — brief failure mode #3). A Laplacian residual with scale b symbols has entropy ~log2(2*e*b) bits; for well-predicted sensor data b is typically 1-4 symbols, i.e. 2.5-4.5 bits/symbol instead of 8. SZ3 wins precisely because it does linear quantization THEN entropy coding of a peaky integer stream; TRACQ currently does non-linear quantization then entropy-codes a flat stream. Rate-distortion theory says a uniform quantizer followed by entropy coding is within 0.25 bits of the optimal entropy-constrained quantizer for smooth densities — companding buys nothing once you have a real entropy stage, and actively costs ~4 bits/symbol of coding gain.
proposals.expected_gain: At matched RMSE, grid bytes shrink 2-3x on UCI Air Quality style data (8 bits -> ~3-4 bits/symbol through DEFLATE, which gets within ~5-10% of order-0 entropy on peaky byte streams). Paper's Enh-8b+Anchors ratio 0.114 should drop to roughly 0.04-0.06 at equal or better error, finally putting daylight between lossy TRACQ and lossless Delta+Zstd (0.12). On MetroPT-3 (long flat stretches, residuals overwhelmingly 0) entropy can fall below 1 bit/symbol, ratio 0.0297 -> ~0.005-0.01. Also delivers failure-mode-#5's error bound for free: max abs pct error = q_step/2 per step (exact per-point bound when combined with closed-loop coding).
proposals.implementation_sketch: In core_enhanced.py add quantize_residual(bits=8, error_bound=None): (1) compute pct grid as now; (2) per variable choose q_step = 2*error_bound_pct or from a target symbol-range percentile; (3) s = np.round(pct/q_step) with np.clip to [-(2**(bits-1)-2), 2**(bits-1)-2]; overflow mask -> escape symbol, exact values into metadata['escapes'] = {flat_indices, float32 values} (store indices as np.diff varints, values via struct/np.tobytes, base64 in JSON or a side binary chunk); (4) q = (s + 2**(bits-1)).astype(np.uint8/np.uint16). Decode: pct_hat = (q - mid)*q_step, patch escapes, then existing cumprod (or closed-loop recursion). ~80 lines, pure numpy, no new deps; reconstruct_from_quantized grows a 'residual_mode' branch keyed on metadata.
proposals.risk: Two real risks. (a) If prediction stays open-loop, the small q_step errors still compound via cumprod — this proposal's RMSE claims assume closed-loop encoding lands too; standalone it only improves ratio, not the divergence failure. (b) Heavy-tailed pct distributions (Air Quality spikes) produce many escapes; if >2-3% of samples escape, the float32 side-channel eats the gain — mitigate with a two-tier escape (second coarser symbol table) or per-variable q_step tuned so escapes <0.5%. Also the image loses the 'dynamic-range-maximized' look; see viewability note.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Strictly preserved and arguably improved: the artifact is still one uint8/uint16 pixel per (variable, timestep). A well-predicted series renders as flat mid-gray with anomalies as bright/dark deviations — visual anomaly detection gets EASIER because interesting events are now the only high-contrast pixels. For human viewing, an optional gamma/contrast-stretch view (display-only, not stored) recovers detail in the quiet regions.
proposals.interactions: Prerequisite-level synergy with closed-loop coding: closed-loop makes residuals smaller and peakier (better entropy) and turns q_step/2 into a true per-point error bound; do them together. Synergizes with any better predictor (delta-of-delta, cross-channel): better prediction directly shrinks b and thus bits/symbol. Conflicts with the existing mu-law path (mutually exclusive branches; keep mu-law as legacy flag). All other proposals below assume this symbol stream.

proposals.name: P2: Dual-artifact container — Zstd-19 zigzag byte stream as PRIMARY, PNG as a deterministic free VIEW
proposals.mechanism: Split 'what we count as compressed bytes' from 'what a human opens'. Primary artifact: the P1 residual symbols zigzag-mapped to unsigned (z = 2|s| - (s<0)), emitted as a flat bytes object, compressed with zstandard level 19 (window >= grid size). The PNG is NOT stored: it is a pure deterministic function of the decoded symbol grid (q = s + 128), regenerated on demand by a render_view() helper or by a --with-view flag that appends it as an optional chunk. The container (container.py) already supports a Zstd-blob mode per the brief, so this is a formalization: primary = zstd(symbols) + JSON metadata; view = derivable PNG, byte-identical every time because the mapping is bijective.
proposals.why_it_wins: PNG DEFLATE has three structural taxes the primary artifact shouldn't pay: (1) DEFLATE's Huffman coding is bit-aligned static/dynamic Huffman over 286 symbols with 32KB windows — Zstd's FSE/tANS gets ~0.02-0.05 bits/symbol closer to order-0 entropy and its large window catches repeats across the whole grid (periodic daily patterns in UCI data are megabytes apart; DEFLATE literally cannot see them); (2) PNG filter bytes and chunk/CRC overhead; (3) Pillow gives no control over filter choice, so the encoder sometimes picks filters that decorrelate the wrong axis. Empirically Zstd-19 beats zlib-6 by 15-35% on low-entropy byte streams and by more when long-range repeats exist. Zigzag mapping matters because it makes byte values monotone in |residual|, concentrating mass on 0,1,2,... which improves both FSE table efficiency and LZ matchability versus the sign-interleaved 126/127/128/129/130 pattern. Note: do NOT bother with a trained Zstd dictionary — dictionaries pay off for many small independent frames, not one large grid; benchmark honesty demands we say so.
proposals.expected_gain: 20-40% fewer bytes than PNG-DEFLATE on the SAME P1 symbol stream (zlib->zstd-19 typical 15-35%, plus removal of PNG framing, plus long-window wins on periodic data). Multiplied with P1: UCI Air Quality total ratio ~0.03-0.045; MetroPT-3 ~0.004-0.008, which is finally in PAA-1024's ratio neighborhood (0.0007 is still smaller, but PAA destroys per-timestep resolution — TRACQ at 0.005 with per-step fidelity is a defensible Pareto point). Zero RMSE cost: this stage is lossless over the symbols.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In container.py add save_tracq(path, symbols_int, metadata): zz = (np.abs(s)*2 - (s<0)).astype(np.uint8); blob = zstd.ZstdCompressor(level=19, write_content_size=True).compress(zz.tobytes()); write [magic, meta_len, meta_json_utf8, blob]. load_tracq inverts. render_view(symbols, metadata) -> PIL Image via existing ImageCodec.save_png for interoperability. Benchmarks in scripts/realworld_benchmark.py count len(file) of the primary; add a column 'view_bytes' when --with-view is set so reviewers see both numbers. ~60 lines. zstandard already installed.
proposals.risk: Reviewer optics: 'the compressed artifact is no longer literally a PNG'. Mitigation is in the framing: the brief itself blesses 'PNG or Zstd blob', and the view is bit-exact reproducible from the primary (state this as a theorem-ish property in the paper). Technical risk is minimal — the only measurable failure mode is Zstd-19 encode speed (~5-20 MB/s single-thread) hurting the encode-MB/s column; fall back to level 12 or multithreaded compressor if that column matters.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Yes, via the dual-artifact contract: every decoded archive yields the exact per-timestep 2D grid, and render_view() produces a standard grayscale PNG (openable in any viewer) that is a deterministic bijection of the stored symbols — nothing about visual inspection or compressed-domain anomaly detection is lost, it just isn't paid for in the rate column unless the user opts in.
proposals.interactions: Pure downstream of P1 (works on any integer symbol grid, including the legacy mu-law one, but gains are small on flat histograms). Independent of closed-loop/predictor choices. Slight overlap with P3: for 16-bit symbols, apply P3's plane split BEFORE the zstd call inside this container. Replaces, rather than fights, the PNG stage; keep codec.py untouched for the view path.

proposals.name: P3: Byte-plane (MSB/LSB) decomposition for 16-bit mode, compressed per-plane
proposals.mechanism: For 16-bit residual symbols, never compress interleaved uint16 bytes. Split q into hi = (q >> 8).astype(uint8) and lo = (q & 0xFF).astype(uint8) and compress the two planes as separate streams (Zstd per P2, or as a 2-row-stacked 8-bit PNG in pure-PNG mode). With P1 centering at 32768, the hi plane is the constant 128 except where |residual| >= 128 steps — i.e. almost everywhere constant — and RLE/LZ reduces it to near zero bytes. The lo plane carries essentially all the entropy and compresses at its own order-0 rate.
proposals.why_it_wins: Pillow's I;16 PNG stores big-endian byte pairs interleaved: the stream alternates (near-constant hi, noisy lo, hi, lo, ...), which (a) halves effective LZ match lengths, (b) forces one Huffman table to serve two wildly different distributions, and (c) breaks PNG byte-filters, which subtract at 1-byte offsets. Planar separation is the standard fix (same reason TIFF predictors + planar config, and ZFP/SZ-style bit-plane coders, exist). Information-theoretically: H(interleaved byte stream, order-0 per byte) ~= (H(hi)+H(lo))/2 but coded with one mismatched table; separated, hi codes at ~0.01-0.1 bits/byte and lo at its true rate. The 16-bit operating point is exactly where TRACQ's RMSE is competitive, so making 16-bit cheap matters for the rate-distortion frontier.
proposals.expected_gain: 30-50% byte reduction for 16-bit grids versus current I;16 PNG (hi plane collapses from 50% of raw bytes to ~1-3%; lo plane compresses slightly better with a dedicated table). Turns the '16-bit costs 2x the bytes of 8-bit' tradeoff into '~1.05-1.3x for 256x finer quantization', which shifts the whole 16-bit curve left in the rate-distortion plot — this is likely the cheapest way to get a TRACQ point that beats ZFP tol=1e-1 on RMSE at comparable ratio on Air Quality.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Inside P2's save_tracq, branch on symbol dtype: if uint16, compress zstd(hi.tobytes()) and zstd(lo.tobytes()) as two length-prefixed blobs (or one blob of np.concatenate([hi.ravel(), lo.ravel()]) — concatenation alone captures most of the win since Zstd's window spans both). Pure-PNG fallback for the view: vstack([hi, lo]) as a (2*n_vars, n_time-1) uint8 PNG with a metadata flag 'plane_split'. ~25 lines in container.py. Decode: q = hi.astype(uint16)<<8 | lo.
proposals.risk: Low. Only failure mode: if residuals are NOT peaky (bad predictor, mu-law legacy path), hi plane is not constant and the split gains little (~5%) — it never hurts, since two Zstd streams of a random split cost at most a few hundred bytes of framing. The 16-bit PNG view under plane-split is a stacked two-panel image rather than a single I;16 image; keep the I;16 render as the human view and the split only in the primary stream.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Fully: the stored symbols reassemble to the exact (n_vars, n_time-1) uint16 grid, and render_view() still emits the standard 16-bit grayscale PNG. The optional stacked hi/lo PNG is itself viewable (hi plane visually flags where large jumps occurred — a bonus inspection channel).
proposals.interactions: Multiplies with P1 (centering is what makes the hi plane constant) and lives inside P2's container. Irrelevant to 8-bit mode. No conflict with closed-loop or predictors. If a future arithmetic/rANS coder is added, plane split becomes unnecessary for it but harmless.

proposals.name: P4: WebP-lossless as the drop-in PNG replacement when a single-file image IS required
proposals.mechanism: For deployments where the artifact must literally be one standards-viewable image file (no dual-artifact allowed), swap PNG for WebP-lossless via Pillow (img.save(buf, format='WEBP', lossless=True, quality=100, method=6)) for 8-bit grids. WebP-lossless replaces PNG's 5 scanline filters + DEFLATE with 14 spatial predictors chosen per 32x32 tile, a color-cache, and LZ77 + canonical Huffman over 2D-aware distances.
proposals.why_it_wins: On synthetic/low-texture imagery (which a P1 mid-gray residual grid is), WebP-lossless is consistently 20-35% smaller than optimized PNG in published corpus tests (Google's benchmark: ~26% average vs libpng, more vs Pillow's non-optimized encoder). Its per-tile predictor selection approximates the 'choose the best PNG filter per row' optimization Pillow denies us, and the color cache is effectively an MTF/RLE hybrid that eats long mid-gray runs cheaply. This is the highest gain available with a ~5-line change and zero container redesign.
proposals.expected_gain: 15-30% fewer bytes than the current Pillow PNG on 8-bit grids (both legacy mu-law and P1 symbols; larger relative gain on P1's peaky grids). It will NOT match P2's Zstd path on long-range-periodic data (WebP window is limited) — expect P2 to beat it by ~10-20% — so position it as the 'strict single-image mode', not the headline number. No RMSE change (lossless over symbols).
proposals.implementation_sketch: In codec.py add save_webp/load_webp mirroring save_png (metadata goes in WebP XMP chunk via img.save(..., xmp=meta_json) or, simpler and safer, a sidecar-free approach: embed meta JSON in an EXIF UserComment; Pillow round-trips both). Guard: WebP-lossless is 8-bit only — raise for uint16 and fall back to PNG or P3's stacked-plane 8-bit representation. Benchmark as a codec column in scripts/realworld_benchmark.py. ~40 lines.
proposals.risk: Three: (a) no 16-bit support — the mode where TRACQ's RMSE is competitive — limiting this to the 8-bit operating points; (b) Pillow's WebP metadata handling is fussier than PNG tEXt (test round-trip of large JSON, else keep a tiny sidecar or trailing bytes after the WebP file payload); (c) 'method=6' encode is slow (~1-5 MB/s), dragging the encode-throughput column. AVIF-lossless was considered and rejected: pillow-avif plugin dependency, slower still, and AV1 lossless rarely beats WebP-lossless on grayscale synthetic content.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Strongest of all proposals: the artifact IS a standard image file that every browser and viewer opens directly; grayscale per-timestep grid semantics unchanged.
proposals.interactions: Alternative to (not composable with) P2's container for the primary artifact; composes fully with P1 (and benefits from it). If P2 is accepted, P4's role shrinks to 'render_view() can optionally emit WebP instead of PNG to make even the view small'. Skip P4 entirely if reviewers accept the dual-artifact framing — it is the insurance policy.

overall_assessment: P1 (centered small-step residual symbols) matters most — nothing else in the entropy stage can work while mu-law companding deliberately flattens the symbol histogram to ~8 bits/symbol; every downstream coder is fighting a distribution engineered to be incompressible. The combination I would ship: P1 + P2 + P3 as one coherent redesign (linear-step centered residual quantizer -> zigzag map -> byte-plane split for 16-bit -> Zstd-19 primary blob, with a deterministic PNG render_view() preserving the image artifact), and P4 held in reserve as the strict single-image fallback mode. Expected combined effect at matched RMSE: ~3-5x byte reduction versus today's PNG path (UCI Air Quality ratio 0.114 -> ~0.03-0.045; MetroPT-3 0.0297 -> ~0.005), plus a genuine user-specifiable per-step error bound (q_step/2) that answers failure mode #5. One honesty caveat the paper must carry: these entropy gains fix the RATIO axis, but the 3-5 order-of-magnitude RMSE gap to ZFP/SZ3 is a prediction/closed-loop problem — the entropy stage must land together with closed-loop encoding (which also makes P1's residuals peakier and its error bound exact) or TRACQ improves its ratio while still losing the distortion axis. Benchmark against zfpy tolerance mode, PAA, Gorilla, and Delta+Zstd using primary-artifact bytes, reporting view bytes separately.
